args: sam variants --help
exit: 0
--- stdout
Annotate mutations relative to a reference from alignments in SAM format

Example usage:
	gofasta sam variants -s aligned.sam -r reference.fasta -a annotation.gb -o variants.csv
	gofasta sam variants -s aligned.sam -r reference.fasta -a annotation.gff -o variants.csv

If --samfile and --outfile are not given, the SAM file is read from stdin and the variants are written to
stdout.

--reference should be the same sequence that was used to make the --samfile alignment, and should be in the
same coordinates as the annotation (--annotation, --genbank or --gff). You don't have to provide a file to
--reference if your annotation has the fasta record in it.

gff-format annotations must be valid version 3 files. See github.com/virus-evolution/gofasta for more details
of the format.

Mutations are annotated with ins (insertion), del (deletion), aa (amino acid change) or nuc (a nucleotide
change that isn't in a codon that is represented by an amino acid change). The formats are:

	ins:2028:3 - a 3-base insertion immediately after (1-based) position 2028 in reference coordinates
	del:11288:9 - a 9-base deletion whose first missing nucleotide is at (1-based) position 11288 in reference coordinates
	aa:S:D614G - the amino acid at (1-based) residue 614 in the S gene is a D in the reference and a G in this sequence
	aa:S:H69- - the amino acid at (1-based) residue 69 in the S gene is an H in the reference and is deleted in this sequence
	aa:S:214EPE - the amino acids EPE are inserted immediately after (1-based) residue 214 in the S gene in this sequence
	nuc:C3037T - the nucleotide at (1-based) position 3037 in reference coordinates is a C in the reference and a T in this sequence

With --group-aa, the amino acid changes from one indel are one entry: aa:S:HV69-- instead of aa:S:H69-|aa:S:V70-.

An indel that shifts the reading frame of a coding sequence is reported only as an indel, as are the indels
after it in that coding sequence, unless indels within 3 codons of it restore the frame. Changes of single
bases are still reported codon by codon.

Usage:
  gofasta sam variants [flags]

Flags:
  -s, --samfile string      SAM file to read (default "stdin")
  -r, --reference string    Reference fasta file used to make the --samfile alignment
  -a, --annotation string   GenBank or GFF3 annotation file, with suffix: .gb, .gbk, .gbff, .gff or .gff3 [.gz] (required, unless --genbank or --gff)
      --genbank string      GenBank annotation file, with any file extension (instead of --annotation)
      --gff string          GFF3 annotation file, with any file extension (instead of --annotation)
  -o, --outfile string      Where to write the variants (default "stdout")
      --start int           Only report mutations with a reference base at or after this position
      --end int             Only report mutations with a reference base at or before this position
      --aggregate           Report the frequency of each mutation
      --threshold float     If --aggregate, only report mutations with a freq greater than or equal to this value
      --append-snps         Report the codon's SNPs in parenthesis after each amino acid change
      --group-aa            Report the amino acid changes from one indel as one entry (aa:S:HV69-- instead of aa:S:H69-|aa:S:V70-)
      --strict              Stop with an error at the first record that can't be processed, instead of warning and skipping it
  -t, --threads int         Number of threads (and CPUs) to use (with no flag, all CPUs are used)
  -h, --help                help for variants
--- stderr
